title: YMTC Files for Landmark IPO After Climbing to No. 3 in Global NAND Race, With DRAM Next
key_facts: Counterpoint Research says Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC), China's only NAND flash maker at commercial scale, has filed for an IPO on Shanghai's STAR Market; the prospectus was filed in August 2026.
YMTC rose to No. 3 globally by NAND shipment volume in Q2 2026, behind Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix and ahead of Kioxia and Micron (Counterpoint Memory Tracker).
Its global NAND revenue share rose from 9% in Q1 2025 to 14% in Q1 2026, with year-on-year revenue growth as high as 478%.
Counterpoint estimates server-related revenue, effectively zero in 2024, will reach close to 39% of YMTC's total revenue by 2028.
MS Hwang, Counterpoint research director: the bigger question is whether YMTC can win design wins with customers outside China.
YMTC's valuation and offer price have not yet been set; CXMT, its DRAM counterpart, listed on the STAR Market on 16 July 2026.
YMTC is researching DRAM (16Gb LPDDR5 testing since October 2025) but has never mass-produced it at scale.
quote_evidence: The Wuhan-based chipmaker rose to No. 3 globally by shipment volume in the second quarter of 2026, according to Counterpoint Research's Memory Tracker and Forecast, now trailing only Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix and moving ahead of Japan's Kioxia and US-based Micron Technology.
YMTC filed its Shanghai STAR Market IPO prospectus in August 2026, following its pre-IPO counselling (tutoring) registration and first-phase progress report earlier in the year.
YMTC's own valuation and offer price have not yet been set.
why_it_matters_hint: A fast-growing Chinese memory maker is gaining share at a time of memory shortages that raise device prices.
event_date: 13 Oct 2026 (Counterpoint analysis); the IPO prospectus was filed in August 2026
notes: The IPO filing itself dates from August 2026, so the news today is Counterpoint's market ranking and analysis, not the filing. Ranking and forecasts are one research firm's estimates. Our 6 Oct edition carried a report on YMTC expecting shortages to last three more years.
